cards.headline: White takes the ko first and can ignore Black's first retake, so Black needs two more ko threats than White: S[KO-2], not S[KO-].

diagrams.caption: The tree's line. After Black 7 it is White's move, and the tree marks the leaf S[KO-].

diagrams.caption: White 8 ataris the Black stone at A18, and Black 9 must fill an outside liberty at once. White 10 takes the ko. Black 11 retakes after a threat, but White 12 ignores it: Black 13 has to fill White's last outside liberty, and White 14 retakes for free.
If Black 9 plays elsewhere, White 10 takes the ko. White still has both outside liberties, so when Black 11 retakes, White 12 fills the shared liberty and wins the race: ALIVE.
The tree's KO− needs White to waste the move at the leaf (White 8 plays elsewhere). Then Black 9 and Black 11 fill both outside liberties, and White 12 takes the ko first: a direct ko, KO−.

text: At the leaf (Diagram 1), Black 1, Black 3 and Black 7 are in a capturing race with White's group, and the ko is in the corner. White 8 in Diagram 2 is White's best move; every other White move gives only KO− or DEAD. Black 9 must then fill one of White's two outside liberties; either one will do. If Black plays elsewhere, White wins the race (Diagram 3); Black's other local replies are self-atari.

In Diagram 2, White 10 takes the ko first. White still has a spare liberty, so White 12 ignores Black 11; Black 13 has to fill that liberty, and White 14 retakes for free. Black has spent one threat and now faces a direct ko that White took first, so Black needs two more threats than White: S[KO-2]. This fits the site tutorial's KO−2: after Black wins it once, it becomes KO−. In approach-ko notation it is S[A-1KO-], the same threat count.

The tree's KO− is right only if White wastes the move at the leaf (Diagram 4). The solver confirms KO−2. In the wider search area, one extra threat for Black stayed undecided even at a million nodes; a reviewer reads it as failing, since neither side has a local ko threat.
